note: Pass/fail targets for scripts/audio/metrics.py. docs/AUDIO.md shows the same table (generated by `metrics.py --targets-table`; a unit test keeps the two identical). 'fail' sets exit code 1; 'warn' is reported only.

common.why: the video pipeline and Remotion run at 48 kHz
DC wastes headroom and clicks at edits
no sample may reach full scale
ffmpeg and the numpy meter should agree; a gap means an odd file
a persistent 50/60 Hz peak (with harmonics) means mains hum in a recording

standalone.description: music heard on its own (trailer, end card, channel music)

checks.why: -14 LUFS-I, YouTube's widely reported reference (not an official spec)
-1 dBTP leaves room for lossy encoding overshoot
below about 8 dB the transients are squashed
negative correlation cancels on phones and mono speakers
the mono fold-down must not lose more than 3 dB
bass below 150 Hz should be mono
overall tilt near pink (-3 dB/oct); typical mixes sit at -3 to -5
2-5 kHz excess is fatiguing on phone speakers and earbuds
200-500 Hz excess sounds boxy and masks speech
500-1000 Hz excess sounds boxy or honky (the reference's first mix read +6)
8-16 kHz floor: hiss louder than this is never acceptable; the reference trio's hats and cymbals read about -62 (the estimate is an upper bound)

sting.description: intro stings, jingles, logo hits (a few seconds)

checks.why: -16 LUFS-I: matches speech-led content without jumping out
-1 dBTP leaves room for lossy encoding overshoot
negative correlation cancels on phones and mono speakers
the mono fold-down must not lose more than 3 dB
2-5 kHz excess is fatiguing on phone speakers and earbuds
200-500 Hz excess sounds boxy
500-1000 Hz excess sounds boxy or honky
a sting must end cleanly, not on a cut

bed.description: music under narration; ducked further in the video mix

checks.why: about -26 LUFS-S: roughly 12 LU under -14 LUFS narration before ducking
no section may climb toward the voice
headroom for summing with voice and SFX
even dynamics make ducking predictable
the 1-4 kHz pocket where speech intelligibility lives
200-500 Hz excess masks the voice's body
negative correlation cancels on phones and mono speakers
the mono fold-down must not lose more than 3 dB
hiss under a quiet bed is exposed when the voice pauses (the reference bed reads about -74)
a seam much sharper than the 50 ms around it is a cut waveform (a click)
loops should not jump in level at the seam

sfx.description: whooshes, pops, keyboard clicks and other one-shots

checks.why: -1 dBTP leaves room for lossy encoding overshoot
the sound should start within 5 ms so it syncs to the frame it is placed on
one-shots must end cleanly, not on a cut
hiss around a one-shot is audible when it is layered
